title: Change Rehearsal Runbook: Safety Harness for Large-Scale Platform Rollouts
author: Sofia Ramirez
body:
Summary:

This runbook describes the Change Rehearsal Safety Harness: an operator-guided, event-sourced rehearsal and automated-safety layer that validates large-scale platform rollouts before hitting production traffic. The harness creates reproducible, reversible rehearsals that exercise the same traffic topology, telemetry, and failure modes as a real rollout while preserving customer isolation and SLO guarantees.

When to use this runbook:
- Major runtime or allocator changes that affect batching, KV cache sharding, or tenant placement.
- Model-variant rollouts that change memory/latency profiles at scale.
- Cross-region routing changes or capacity pool rebalances.
- Any rollout where the expected SLO delta is > 5% (latency or error rate).

Scope and goals:
- Validate operational correctness of rollout steps end-to-end.
- Detect regressions in token latency, tail latency, and cost signals.
- Provide a clear abort/rollback decision path with automated safeties.
- Produce a post-rehearsal artifact: reproducible traffic trace, operator checklist, and metric diff report.

Owner and escalation:
- Primary owner: Platform Release Engineering (eng-platform-release).
- On-call escalation: Platform SRE (primary) -> Runtime Team (secondary) -> Eng Manager (tertiary).
- Pager duty play: page the on-call channel when automated abort triggers.

Prerequisites (pre-rehearsal checklist):
1) Rehearsal configuration reviewed and checked into the rehearsal registry. Required fields: rehearsal_id, target_services, sample_cohorts, timeframe, abort_criteria, visibility_tenants.
2) Canary dataset and traffic seed verified in the Synthetic Tenant Fabric (see Synthetic Tenant Fabric catalog).
3) Observability dashboard and alert set exists and is linked in the rehearsal plan (add below).
4) Target environments: rehearsal-stage (isolated), rehearsal-mirror (mirrors production routing), and production (for final progressive gates).
5) Owner and runbook call list published in the rehearsal plan.

Rehearsal safety harness components (high level):
- Traffic replayer: event-sourced replayer that can replay requests at scaled QPS while preserving prefix/KV distributions.
- Read-only operator toggles: allows safe flip of routing for rehearsal cohorts without mutating live customer state.
- Automated monitors: guard rails that evaluate SLO deltas continuously and can trigger automated aborts.
- Audit logger: immutable trace for each rehearsal step (who, when, config).

Rehearsal run workflow (operator steps):
1) Prepare the rehearsal plan document including expected metric baselines and risk matrix. Attach plan to the deployment ticket.
2) Stage rehearsals in rehearsal-stage: run a low-rate replay to validate connectivity and traces (10–20% of target QPS).
3) Expand to rehearsal-mirror: increase to 50% of planned production sample. Observe synthetic tenants and cost signals.
4) Trigger smoke assertions: run pre-defined prompt/response checks (examples provided below).
5) Execute progressive gating: move cohorts in 10% increments with 30-minute steady-state windows.
6) If all gates pass, schedule a controlled production ramp following the same increment policy and operator approvals.

Abort criteria (automated and operator-visible):
- Latency: 95th percentile request latency increases by >= 30% over baseline for 10 consecutive minutes.
- Tail: 99th percentile latency exceeds baseline + 200ms for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Errors: client-visible 5xx rate increases by >= 0.5% absolute over baseline.
- Quality: model hallucination/regression alerts fire more than threshold for the prompt-set (see quality guardrail below).
- Cost shock: token cost per request increases by >= 10% sustained for 10 minutes.
- Operator manual abort: any on-call engineer may abort if unexpected behavior observed.

Automated safety actions (if any abort criteria met):
- Step A: Pause traffic replayer and mark the rehearsal cohort as failed.
- Step B: Trigger rollback automation to previous stable routing variant.
- Step C: Notify on-call Slack channel and create incident placeholder with rehearsal_id tag.

Instrumentation and dashboards: (minimum required)
- Rehearsal Overview dashboard (Grafana): rehearshal_id, cohort_id, QPS, 50/95/99 latencies, 5xx rate, token-cost-per-request, KV cache hit ratio, model-ops memory pressure.
- Diff panel: live baseline vs rehearsal delta for each metric.
- Trace panel: representative traces for synthetic tenants and a sample of customer requests.
- Alert rules (Prometheus/Alertmanager): rehearsal_abnormal_latency, rehearsal_error_spike, rehearsal_cost_spike.

Example Grafana query snippets (PromQL-like pseudo):
- 95th latency (ms): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{rehearsal_id=~"$rehearsal"}[5m])) by (le)) * 1000
- 5xx rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..", rehearsal_id=~"$rehearsal"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{rehearsal_id=~"$rehearsal"}[5m]))

Synthetic smoke tests (executable checks):
- Prompt-set 1: latency_assertion("translate-short", max_latency=200ms)
- Prompt-set 2: semantic_consistency_check("qa-pairs", min_similarity=0.85)
- KV cache check: verify cache hit ratio for prefix cohort > 60% (within 2% of baseline).

Example CLI: enable rehearsal cohort (operator):
$ platformctl rehearsal create --id=rr-2026-11 --cohort=synthetic-llm-small --qps-target=120 --duration=60m --rollback-variant=variant-v1
$ platformctl rehearsal start --id=rr-2026-11

Quick abort (operator):
$ platformctl rehearsal abort --id=rr-2026-11 --reason="99p latency spike observed"

Rehearsal configuration example (JSON blob):
{
  "rehearsal_id": "rr-2026-11",
  "target_services": ["runtime-proxy", "kv-prefix-cache", "model-swapper"],
  "sample_cohorts": ["synthetic-llm-small", "shadow-tier-a"],
  "qps_profile": "ramp-10-50-100",
  "abort_criteria": ["95p+30pct","5xx+0.5pct","token-cost+10pct"],
  "visibility_tenants": ["internal-test-1","synthetic-tenant-2"]
}

Post-rehearsal reporting and artifacts (required):
- Rehearsal summary: one-paragraph executive summary, pass/fail, duration, peak QPS.
- Metric diff CSV: baseline vs rehearsal for 1/50/95/99 latencies, error rates, token cost, cache hit ratio.
- Trace archive: link to archived replay trace (s3://rehearsal-traces/rr-2026-11.trace).
- Incident ticket if any aborts occurred with root-cause hypothesis.

Postmortem template (minimum fields):
- rehearsal_id: string
- summary: short paragraph
- pass_fail: PASS | FAIL
- top_observations: bullet list
- root_cause: short paragraph
- remediation_actions: numbered list with owners and due dates

Risk matrix (example):
| Risk area | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Owner |
|-----------|------------|--------|------------|-------|
| KV cache inconsistency | Medium | High | Read-only rehearsal mode, cache-cohort fencing | Runtime Team |
| Model memory OOM | Low | High | memory-safety-limits, abort_on_memory_growth | Model Ops |
| Billing anomaly | Low | Medium | cost smoke checks, token-cost abort | Billing Eng |

Best practices and operator tips:
- Always pair a rehearsal with a short (1–2hr) blackout window for rapid operator action.
- Reuse the same synthetic cohorts across related rollouts to make comparisons meaningful.
- Keep rehearsal durations short for each increment; prefer more increments over longer windows.
- Maintain a rehearsal registry with tags for model family, allocator version, and kernel profile.

Appendix: links and references:
- Rehearsal registry (internal): /wiki/rehearsal-registry
- Synthetic Tenant Fabric: /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/synthetic-tenant-fabric-catalog-2025
- Canary orchestration DSL: /confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/canary-orchestration-dsl-and-safe-rollback-playbook-2026

Change history:
- 2025-11-12: Created by Sofia Ramirez (initial draft).
- 2026-01-15: Updated thresholds and added automated abort steps (Marcus Chen).

Notes: This runbook emphasizes reproducibility and safety. It is intended to sit alongside existing canary and rollout playbooks but focuses explicitly on rehearsals driven by event-sourced replays and an auditable safety harness.
